comment: Which sources a wiki expansion may lean on, in preference order. This is editorial policy — who to trust — and is deliberately separate from web-research's search provider registry, which is about how to reach a given source. A source that names a 'provider' is resolved through that registry: the site's own API or published index, asked by web-research so that one implementation serves every caller. That is preferred over general web search because it keeps working when the engines behind SearXNG rate-limit the instance, and because a site's own index knows its entry titles, so a wrong hit is rejected before anything is downloaded. A source with no 'provider' falls back to site-restricted search pinned to SearXNG, since 'site:' is SearXNG syntax and means nothing to a direct API. Four of those sources publish no API at all, and PhilPapers answers HTTP 403 to every non-browser client, so there is nothing to route them to. Candidates come back unranked and are matched here: a URL is never guessed, because SEP entry slugs are topic-based rather than name-based and there is no /entries/latour/ to construct. Lower 'authority' is tried first. 'kinds' and 'topics' accept '*' to match everything.

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed and stable. The strongest source available for anything in the philosophy cluster.

sources.label: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed. Often covers a figure the SEP has no standalone entry for.

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (Buddhist philosophy)
sources.notes: Separate entry so a Sanskrit or Pali term is searched with its tradition named.

sources.label: PhilPapers
sources.notes: Best for pinning a work to an author and year. Metadata rather than full text.

sources.label: Encyclopaedia Britannica
sources.notes: Edited and citable. Preferred over Wikipedia for places, events, and historical figures.

sources.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (science)
sources.notes: Covers philosophy of science and mathematics terms that general encyclopedias treat only technically.

sources.label: PubMed
sources.notes: Use the abstract only. A wiki definition should not rest on a single primary study.

sources.label: MeSH
sources.notes: Controlled biomedical vocabulary — well suited to a glossary-shaped term note.

sources.label: Oxford Reference
sources.notes: Often paywalled past the definition line; treat a short extract as metadata-level evidence.

sources.label: Wikipedia
sources.notes: The universal fallback and usually the only source with dates for a contemporary figure. Ranked last on purpose: it is the source most likely to be right and least likely to be citable, so prefer anything above it when both resolve.
